cs.t: I've been using a Kensington Expert Mouse Trackball for several years now. You might like it for a center trackball position. The ball comes out really easy so it's easy to take apart and clean. cs.t: Around the turn of the century, my years of web dev work started taking a toll on my carpal tunnel. Some research led me to track balls (Kensington Expert Mouse) and the DVORAK layout. I managed to convert quickly enough to never have a truly bad flare up, and to this day I am rocking that layout. Pro tip: once you have committed, you can get a hard-coded DVORAK keyboard from UNICOMP, who make modern versions of the IBM Model M buckling-spring keyboard (which is often called a “desk yacht” due to its massive size). This allows you to have DVORAK without having to mess with your system’s default keyboard, and allow you to type on other people’s systems by just dragging your keyboard along. You need to add a customization to your order and specify DVORAK, but the keyboards are absolutely spectacular and last for many years. Be sure to also pick up the keyboard protector if you are not keen on breaking it down twice a year just to clean it. The plastic protector is low-end lame, as it is not exactly form-fitting (vacuum-moulded instead of form moulded), but it is better than nothing.
Kensington make multiple trackballs that are ambidextrous. I use both the wireless and wired (on laptop and desktop respectively) versions of their “Expert Mouse” model for a fair few years now.

cs.t: Exactly, Expert Mouse = ring, Slimblade = the ball itself. In Slimblade you can scroll from your neutral hand position, that's what sells it to me. I've owned a Slimblade for 10 years, have tried all sorts of trackballs, and I can't imagine anything better for daily use. I got the KEM for work, but requiring hand adjustment to scroll feels like a definite step back, so I sent it back and ordered a second Slimblade instead.
